raw_response:
Well, I've been working these fields for 25 years now, so I mostly do what I know works. My 72 mu is big, and with just me and my wife at home and the kids working in town, I can't fuss over every little thing. I plant mostly cotton like I always do — cotton is what sells around here and what I understand. I'll put about 60 mu in cotton and the other 12 mu in sunflower along the edges and in the saltier patch where cotton doesn't do as well.

For cotton I buy the Bt seed — the kind that fights bollworm. Everyone around here uses it, and I don't want to go back to spraying every week like we did when I was young. I buy the seed from the same dealer in town. For fertilizer I use compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) as base, about 2 bags per mu before planting, then topdress with urea when the buds show, maybe another half bag per mu. That works out to around 18 kg of nitrogen, 8 of phosphorus, 8 of potash per mu. A little more than the book says maybe, but I'd rather have too much than watch the bolls drop. Losing yield hurts more than an extra bag of urea.

I'll plough the cotton ground in early spring — cotton needs deep soil, rotary alone is not enough. I water from my well about 4 times: once after planting if the rain doesn't come, then at budding, flowering, and boll-setting. Pesticide I still spray maybe 6 times even with Bt seed — for aphids, spider mites, and the plant bugs that Bt doesn't touch. Last year I got about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton, so I expect similar this year.

For sunflower I don't spend much. It's a tough crop, handles the salty soil. I use rotary tillage, drop the seed, put on about 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu and that's it. Water maybe twice. Spray once or twice for the moth that eats the head. I get around 220 kg per mu usually.
